title: 1952 Farnborough Airshow DH.110 crash
summary: During an aerobatic display at the Farnborough Airshow, a prototype de Havilland DH.110 jet disintegrated in flight. Following a supersonic dive and flypast from 40,000 feet and during a left bank at about 450 knots toward the crowd, the pilot pulled up into a climb. In less than a second, the outer sections of the wing, both engines and the cockpit separated from the airframe. Debris fell onto spectators, killing 29 and injuring 60. The investigation showed the wing had only 64% of its intended strength.
probable_cause: Structural failure due to a design flaw in the wing's leading edge, with the outer section of the wing failing because it had only 64% of its intended strength.

events.text: Display began with a supersonic dive and flypast from 40,000 feet
During a left bank at about 450 knots toward the air show's spectators, the pilot pulled up into a climb
In less than a second, the aircraft disintegrated: the outer sections of the wing, both engines and the cockpit separated from the airframe
The cockpit fell in front of spectators, debris scattered, one engine ploughed into Observation Hill causing most of the 29 spectator fatalities
